items.title: New monthly price takes effect
items.quote: ab dem 01.01.2027 kostet Ihr Tarif monatlich 16,99 € statt bisher 14,99 €.
items.computation: The letter states the new price applies from a fixed calendar date, so this date is used as written, no counting needed.

items.title: Exercise special right to cancel the contract because of the price increase
items.quote: Für diese Kündigung haben Sie drei Monate Zeit, gerechnet ab dem Zugang dieser Mitteilung; wirksam wird sie frühestens an dem Tag, an dem der neue Preis gilt.
items.computation: This is a private company letter, not an authority, so the statutory 4-day Bekanntgabefiktion for authorities (§ 122 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 AO / § 37 Abs. 2 SGB X) does not apply, and the letter gives no separate 'zur Post gegeben am' posting date. The exact day of actual receipt (Zugang i.S.d. § 130 BGB) is therefore not stated. As the letter is dated Saturday 21.11.2026 and the customer already has it in hand on 24.11.2026 (today), I assume, as the earliest plausible and most conservative estimate, ordinary postal transit of about 3 calendar days, giving an assumed Zugang on Tuesday 24.11.2026. Counting the 3-month period from that day of receipt (day of event not separately added, per §§ 187/188 BGB month-counting: same day-number n months later), 3 months after 24.11.2026 is 24.02.2027 (Wednesday, not a weekend or NW public holiday, so no § 193 BGB shift is needed). The notice of cancellation itself must reach the provider by this date; it then takes effect at the earliest on 01.01.2027, the day the new price starts.

warnings: The exact date on which this letter was actually received (Zugang) by the customer is not stated anywhere in the letter; the three-month deadline to exercise the special termination right is counted from that unknown Zugang date, so the computed due date of 2027-02-24 rests on an assumed ~3-day postal transit from the printed letter date (21.11.2026) and should be verified against the customer's actual postmark/receipt date if available.
The amounts 14.99 and 16.99 are the old and new monthly tariff prices set by this price-increase notice, not a payment currently due.
